title: TCGCSV-first variant expansion (schema + algorithm rework, full reset)
description:
Take TCGCSV as the authoritative source for which printings a card has, instead of bootstrapping from pokemontcg.io price keys + rarity heuristics. Audit showed 130+ fabricated reverse_holo printings in ASC alone and BLK cards with non-existent 'normal' printings.

Bigger goal (added per user feedback): no conditional logic in the application to compensate for a bad data model or shitty data. The right answer is to make the data right and let the SQL queries be straightforward.

Schema changes (edit V1 directly — user has authorized a full wipe, no migration history to preserve):
1. New tcgcsv_products table: (product_id PK, group_id, name, collector_number, derived_variant). Populated by import_tcgcsv so expansion can query the full product list without holding it in memory.
2. printings gets a sub_type_name column. Set at expansion time from the TCGplayer sub_type the variant maps to. Price queries then become a simple JOIN — no CASE expressions, no IS NULL OR fallbacks.

Algorithm:
- import_tcgcsv runs BEFORE variant expansion and persists products + prices.
- derive_variants_from_tcgcsv(card): for the card's set group + collector number, list TCGCSV products. For each base product, emit one printing per advertised sub_type (Normal → normal, Reverse Holofoil → reverse_holo, Holofoil → holo, ...). For each pattern product (Master Ball / Energy Symbol / etc.), emit one printing of that pattern variant. Each printing knows its product_id and its sub_type_name.
- expand_all_printings: TCGCSV-derived first; if a card has no TCGCSV products (brand-new set TCGCSV hasn't fetched), fall back to a minimal 'just normal' bootstrap. Layer-3 overlay still applies on top for true exceptions (stamps, manual additions).

Code to delete:
- VARIANT_PRICE_SUBTYPE CASE constant (no longer needed once printings carry sub_type_name).
- IS NULL OR sub_type filter pattern at each call site.
- bootstrap_from_rarity's release_date pre-LC reverse-holo check (TCGCSV tells us what exists, not the year).
- variant_from_product_name + auto-create logic in link_card_printings — gets pulled into the new derive step.

Process:
1. V1 migration: add tcgcsv_products, add sub_type_name to printings.
2. Implement derive_variants_from_tcgcsv + new expand_all_printings.
3. Reorder data.rs refresh: TCGCSV first, then expand.
4. Simplify all price subqueries.
5. Tests: ASC patterns (Energy Symbol/Quick Ball); ASC C/U/R that should NOT get plain RH; BLK with no Normal sub_type; pre-LC commons; overlay still wins.
6. Teardown prod volume + reseed; spot-check ASC Dreepy, BLK Klink, 151 Bulbasaur, WHT Swadloon, base1 commons.
close_reason: Closed

title: Move variant display metadata into a shared.sqlite `variants` table
description: Variant display data (label, sort rank, chip color, short table tag) currently lives in four scattered TS/Svelte functions plus a Rust KNOWN_VARIANTS constant. Move all of it into a single shared.sqlite table seeded from data/variants.json at `pkdump setup` time. Add a FK from printings.variant so ingest can no longer silently introduce unknown codes.
design:
Schema:
- variants(code PK, label, short, rank, color) — all NOT NULL
- printings.variant becomes FK -> variants(code)

Source of truth: data/variants.json (flat list of {code,label,short,rank,color} records). pkdump setup re-seeds the table (DELETE + INSERT) so the file is authoritative.

API: GET /api/variants returns the full list. Frontend fetches once on first need and caches in a /variants.svelte.ts store; the four display functions collapse to map lookups.

Migrations:
- shared migration N: CREATE TABLE variants ... + seed (initial rows so the FK can be added)
- shared migration N+1: ALTER printings ADD constraint (or rebuild via temp table — SQLite has no direct ADD FK).

Removes the 'Rh → Reverse Holo' stopgap in variantLabel() since the label is now data.

title: link_card_printings flattens multi-product-per-card pricing
description:
tcgcsv::link_card_printings runs UPDATE printings SET tcgplayer_product_id = ?1 WHERE card_id = ?2 — so all variants of a card end up pointing to the SAME TCGplayer product, whichever the linker processed last. TCGplayer actually has separate products per pattern (Holo vs Reverse Holo vs Poke Ball vs Master Ball vs Trainer Gallery), each with its own pricing. Today, pokeball_rh and masterball_rh printings for 151 / Prismatic Evolutions share the price (and the new card-detail price-history chart) of the base printing, not their actual market.

Fix scope:
1. Match TCGplayer products to a specific printing variant, not just to a card. TCGplayer's extendedData typically carries hints (e.g. 'Number' with a suffix, or product name containing 'Master Ball'). Need to parse those and route to the right printing_id.
2. Schema is already OK — printings.tcgplayer_product_id is per-printing — just the linker logic is too coarse.
3. After the fix, re-run 'pkdump data refresh' to relink.

Order-of-operations matters: should land before any user-facing UI that promises per-pattern pricing.

title: Bogus reverse_holo printings on pre-Legendary-Collection sets (base1…base5)

Threads through expand_variants → expand_all_printings (which already SELECTs from cards — just JOIN sets). Then re-run 'pkdump data refresh' on prod to soft-deprecate the wrong rows. title: Hoist variants::ensure_code out of the per-card expansion loop
description:
expand_all_printings now calls pkdump_db::variants::ensure_code inside the per-card transaction, doing a SELECT-then-maybe-INSERT for every (card, variant) pair — ~60k extra round-trips on a full setup (visible as a several-minute slowdown of `pkdump setup` step 5).

Cheap fix: collect the union of variant codes across all cards (overrides + tcgcsv resolutions) once, call ensure_code in a single bulk pass before the per-card loop. The FK then just needs to validate against pre-populated rows.

Also worth: replace the SELECT-then-INSERT in ensure_code with a single INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING (cheaper, no read).

title: Stamped promo variants need cross-group linking (Victini Black Bolt Stamped)
description:
Stamped promos like 'Victini Black Bolt Stamped' (TCGplayer product 668956) live in the 'Pokemon Miscellaneous Cards and Products' TCGCSV group — distinct from the base card's set group. Our link_card_printings only matches products to cards within the same group's bridged set, so:

1. The stamped variant doesn't show in the BLK Victini modal (no stamp_blackbolt printing created)
2. The stamped variant doesn't appear in 'All cards' search (no row in pkdump.cards for it; it isn't a separate pokemontcg.io card either)

Approach options:
- Parse stamped-promo product names (regex 'Card Name Set Stamped' format) and resolve them to the closest base card across all groups, then create a stamp_<set> printing on the base card. Risky — naming is loose.
- Treat the Miscellaneous group specially during link, with a known list of stamp suffixes and a fallback name+rarity matcher.
- Add a manual overlay layer in data/overrides for explicit stamp variants per base card.

Needs product survey (how many Miscellaneous stamps exist, naming consistency) before picking. Defer until pattern-variant work (pokedumpster-NEW1) lands.

title: Pre-LC variants: 1st Edition, Shadowless, Wizards-promo holo/non-holo not modelled
description:
After the reverse_holo cutoff fix (pokedumpster-jmn) the pre-LC era still has variant gaps:

1. 1st Edition vs Unlimited — base1..base5 + gym1/gym2 + neo1..neo4 all shipped in 1st Edition and Unlimited print runs. KNOWN_VARIANTS already has first_ed_holo / first_ed_normal / unlimited_holo, but layer-1 needs pokemontcg.io price-key support (1stEditionHolofoil / 1stEditionNormal / unlimitedHolofoil) AND/OR overlay rules per set+rarity.

2. Shadowless (Base Set first print) — not in KNOWN_VARIANTS at all. Add a 'shadowless_holo' / 'shadowless_normal' code and overlay rules for base1.

3. Wizards Black Star Promos (basep) — current bootstrap assigns 'Promo' rarity → ['holo'] for all 53 cards, but real basep is a mix (e.g. #1 Pikachu is non-holo, #4 Mewtwo is holo). Either thread a rarity-bootstrap-doesn't-fit special case, or write per-card overlays in variant_augmentations.json keyed by set='basep'+number. Probably overlay is the lowest-friction path.

None of these block anyone today — pkdump has no users tracking pre-LC cards. File so the audit history is here when someone does.
close_reason: TCGCSV doesn't publish 1st Edition / Shadowless sub_types for base1..base5 (only Normal + Holofoil), so TCGCSV-first expansion can't surface them. Adding these would require ingesting pokemontcg.io's tcgplayer.prices keys as a secondary source AND a way to price the resulting printings (pokemontcg.io carries the prices but they don't map to a TCGCSV product_id, so the prices table schema would need to accept a non-TCGCSV source). Not blocking anyone — keep the honest 'only what we can price' state. Reopen when a pre-LC collector cares.

title: Per-condition price history (NM vs LP vs MP vs HP vs DMG)
description:
Current prices table has ONE history per (tcgplayer_product_id, sub_type_name, source, price_type, observed_at) — sub_type is finish (Normal/Holo/RH), not condition. NM and LP copies of the same printing share the same chart, which doesn't reflect resale reality. User wants distinct price streams per condition.

Blocked on data sourcing: TCGCSV publishes one market price per product (effectively NM). Need to choose:
  (a) heuristic multipliers on NM (LP ≈ 0.85×, MP ≈ 0.6×, HP ≈ 0.4×, DMG ≈ 0.25×) — cheap, lossy
  (b) per-condition listings from eBay sold / TCGplayer conditional pricing — accurate, more infra

Schema impact when shipped: add a 'condition' column to prices (or a sibling table prices_by_condition), and a UNIQUE that includes it. Likely keep the NM stream + add multiplier-derived rows for other conditions in v1, then swap to real data in v2 when (b) is built.

value: Data model is the product. Anything data-shaped (lookups, labels, ranks, enums, derived display metadata) living in API or frontend code is a smell — flag it immediately. The schema is what lets UI tweaks stay simple and lets edge cases (which will surface as the collection is entered in anger) get fixed in one place. Bias toward: define it as a table or seed file, attach an FK, let display code do nothing but render. Examples found in May 2026: variantLabel/variantRank/variantColor/variantTag scattered across TS while the canonical variant list lived in a Rust constant — fixed by moving to shared.sqlite variants table (pokedumpster-mk4).
